016145: // The result type of an arithmetic operation with at least one complex
016146: // operand: complex, over the usual arithmetic type of the two corresponding
016147: // real types (C11 6.3.1.8p1).
016148: BUSTER_C_INTERNAL IrTypeId c_ir_complex_result_type(CIntegerIrBuilder* builder, IrTypeId left_type, IrTypeId right_type)
016149: {
016150:     IrType* left = ir_type_from_id(&builder->program->types, left_type);
016151:     IrType* right = ir_type_from_id(&builder->program->types, right_type);
016152:     if (!left || !right || (!left->is_complex && !right->is_complex))
016153:     {
016154:         return IR_TYPE_ID_INVALID;
016155:     }
016156:     IrTypeId left_real = left->is_complex ? left->element_type : left_type;
016157:     IrTypeId right_real = right->is_complex ? right->element_type : right_type;
016158:     IrTypeId element = c_ir_usual_arithmetic_type(builder, left_real, right_real);
016159:     return c_ir_complex_type_for_element(builder, element);
016160: }

016162: // `__real__ E` and `__imag__ E` as values. GNU allows either on a real
016163: // operand too: `__real__ x` is `x` and `__imag__ x` is a positive zero of
016164: // x's type, which is what Clang emits, and it is what makes the operators
016165: // usable in code that is generic over real and complex.
016166: BUSTER_C_INTERNAL IrValueId c_ir_emit_complex_part_operator(CIntegerIrBuilder* builder, IrValueId value, bool imaginary, IrSourceRange source)
016167: {
016168:     IrType* complex_type = c_ir_value_complex_type(builder, value);
016169:     if (!complex_type)
016170:     {
016171:         if (value.value >= builder->function->value_count)
016172:         {
016173:             return IR_VALUE_ID_INVALID;
016174:         }
016175:         IrTypeId type_id = builder->function->values[value.value].canonical_type;
016176:         IrType* type = ir_type_from_id(&builder->program->types, type_id);
016177:         if (!type || (type->kind != IR_TYPE_FLOAT && type->kind != IR_TYPE_INTEGER && type->kind != IR_TYPE_BOOLEAN))
016178:         {
016179:             builder->failure_message = S8("__real__ and __imag__ require an arithmetic operand");
016180:             return IR_VALUE_ID_INVALID;
016181:         }
016182:         if (!imaginary)
016183:         {
016184:             return value;
016185:         }
016186:         return type->kind == IR_TYPE_FLOAT ? c_ir_complex_zero(builder, type_id, source)
016187:                                            : c_ir_emit_integer_value_typed(builder, 0, false, (CToken){0}, type_id);
016188:     }
016189:     IrTypeId element = complex_type->element_type;
016190:     IrValueId place = c_ir_complex_operand_place(builder, value, source);
016191:     if (place.value == IR_ID_UNDERLYING_INVALID)
016192:     {
016193:         return IR_VALUE_ID_INVALID;
016194:     }
016195:     return c_ir_complex_part(builder, place, element, imaginary ? 1u : 0u, source);
016196: }

016198: // `+ - * /`, unary `-`, GNU unary `~` (conjugation) and `== !=` where at
016199: // least one operand is complex. Everything else -- the remaining bitwise and
016200: // the relational operators, `%` -- has no complex form in C and is refused
016201: // here rather than silently applied to the real half.
016202: BUSTER_C_INTERNAL bool c_ir_apply_complex_operation(CIntegerIrBuilder* builder, CConditionalOperator operation, IrValueId* values, u32* value_count,
016203:                                                       u32 first, u32 operand_count, IrSourceRange source)
016204: {
016205:     IrTypeId left_type = builder->function->values[values[first].value].canonical_type;
016206:     IrTypeId right_type = operand_count == 2 ? builder->function->values[values[first + 1].value].canonical_type : left_type;
016207:     IrTypeId result_type = c_ir_complex_result_type(builder, left_type, right_type);
016208:     IrType* result_complex = c_ir_complex_type_of(builder, result_type);
016209:     if (!result_complex)
016210:     {
016211:         builder->failure_message = S8("unsupported complex operand type");
016212:         return false;
016213:     }
016214:     IrTypeId element = result_complex->element_type;
016215:     bool left_complex = c_ir_complex_type_of(builder, left_type) != 0;
016216:     bool right_complex = operand_count == 2 && c_ir_complex_type_of(builder, right_type) != 0;
016217:     IrValueId real = IR_VALUE_ID_INVALID;
016218:     IrValueId imaginary = IR_VALUE_ID_INVALID;
016219:     if (operand_count == 1)
016220:     {
016221:         // GNU spells complex conjugation `~` -- C99 Annex G's `conj` -- so the
016222:         // one bitwise operator that has no complex form on a real operand does
016223:         // have one here. It negates the imaginary half alone; unary `-`
016224:         // negates both.
016225:         if (operation != C_CONDITIONAL_UNARY_MINUS && operation != C_CONDITIONAL_BITWISE_NOT)
016226:         {
016227:             builder->failure_message = S8("this unary operator has no complex form");
016228:             return false;
016229:         }
016230:         IrValueId converted = c_ir_emit_cast(builder, values[first], result_type, source);
016231:         if (converted.value == IR_ID_UNDERLYING_INVALID || !c_ir_complex_split(builder, converted, &real, &imaginary, source))
016232:         {
016233:             return false;
016234:         }
016235:         real = operation == C_CONDITIONAL_UNARY_MINUS ? c_ir_emit_unary_value(builder, real, element, IR_UNARY_FLOAT_NEGATE, source) : real;
016236:         imaginary = c_ir_emit_unary_value(builder, imaginary, element, IR_UNARY_FLOAT_NEGATE, source);
016237:         IrValueId negated = c_ir_complex_compose(builder, result_type, real, imaginary, source);
016238:         if (negated.value == IR_ID_UNDERLYING_INVALID)
016239:         {
016240:             return false;
016241:         }
016242:         *value_count = first;
016243:         values[(*value_count)++] = negated;
016244:         return true;
016245:     }
016246:     // Both operands are read before anything is emitted for the operation, so
016247:     // the two splits below cannot interleave with each other's field loads.
016248:     IrValueId left_real = IR_VALUE_ID_INVALID;
016249:     IrValueId left_imaginary = IR_VALUE_ID_INVALID;
016250:     IrValueId right_real = IR_VALUE_ID_INVALID;
016251:     IrValueId right_imaginary = IR_VALUE_ID_INVALID;
016252:     if (left_complex)
016253:     {
016254:         IrValueId converted = c_ir_emit_cast(builder, values[first], result_type, source);
016255:         if (converted.value == IR_ID_UNDERLYING_INVALID || !c_ir_complex_split(builder, converted, &left_real, &left_imaginary, source))
016256:         {
016257:             return false;
016258:         }
016259:     }
016260:     else
016261:     {
016262:         left_real = c_ir_emit_cast(builder, values[first], element, source);
016263:     }
016264:     if (right_complex)
016265:     {
016266:         IrValueId converted = c_ir_emit_cast(builder, values[first + 1], result_type, source);
016267:         if (converted.value == IR_ID_UNDERLYING_INVALID || !c_ir_complex_split(builder, converted, &right_real, &right_imaginary, source))
016268:         {
016269:             return false;
016270:         }
016271:     }
016272:     else
016273:     {
016274:         right_real = c_ir_emit_cast(builder, values[first + 1], element, source);
016275:     }
016276:     if (left_real.value == IR_ID_UNDERLYING_INVALID || right_real.value == IR_ID_UNDERLYING_INVALID)
016277:     {
016278:         return false;
016279:     }
016280:     IrValueId result = IR_VALUE_ID_INVALID;
016281:     switch (operation)
016282:     {
016283:     case C_CONDITIONAL_ADD:
016284:     {
016285:         real = c_ir_emit_binary_value(builder, left_real, right_real, element, IR_BINARY_FLOAT_ADD, source);
016286:         imaginary = left_complex && right_complex
016287:                         ? c_ir_emit_binary_value(builder, left_imaginary, right_imaginary, element, IR_BINARY_FLOAT_ADD, source)
016288:                         : (left_complex ? left_imaginary : right_imaginary);
016289:         result = c_ir_complex_compose(builder, result_type, real, imaginary, source);
016290:         break;
016291:     }
016292:     case C_CONDITIONAL_SUBTRACT:
016293:     {
016294:         real = c_ir_emit_binary_value(builder, left_real, right_real, element, IR_BINARY_FLOAT_SUBTRACT, source);
016295:         if (left_complex && right_complex)
016296:         {
016297:             imaginary = c_ir_emit_binary_value(builder, left_imaginary, right_imaginary, element, IR_BINARY_FLOAT_SUBTRACT, source);
016298:         }
016299:         else if (left_complex)
016300:         {
016301:             imaginary = left_imaginary;
016302:         }
016303:         else
016304:         {
016305:             imaginary = c_ir_emit_unary_value(builder, right_imaginary, element, IR_UNARY_FLOAT_NEGATE, source);
016306:         }
016307:         result = c_ir_complex_compose(builder, result_type, real, imaginary, source);
016308:         break;
016309:     }

016311:     case C_CONDITIONAL_DIVIDE:
016312:     {
016313:         bool divide = operation == C_CONDITIONAL_DIVIDE;
016314:         if (left_complex && !right_complex)
016315:         {

016317:             // complex denominator needs the recovering algorithm.
